title: Sir Geoffrey Wilkinson Lecture 2026 – Towards Solar Fuels and Fertilisers
desc:
Towards Solar Fuels and Fertilisers: Managing Proton and Electron Currency through Molecular Design

Life runs on electrons and protons. Together, or as hydrogen-atom equivalents, they allow plants to store solar energy, underpin the fuels that power society, and help make the fertilisers needed to sustain life.

Simply put, hydrogen atoms decorate many of the key molecular building blocks of our world. Chemists would like to harness this same basic currency to make fuels, fertilisers, and other useful molecules using renewable electricity or light.

The challenge is control. Protons and electrons readily combine to make hydrogen gas, often more easily than they can be directed toward other molecules. Learning how to steer them selectively is therefore a central problem in modern…

desc:
Title

Pick to Learn: state-of-the-art safety guarantees for machine learning and control

Abstract

AI models are increasingly embedded in scientific research and industrial production, where they inform predictions and drive decisions. title: Solving crystal structures with femtosecond time resolution for solid state physics research (LUXD)
desc:
Abstract:

Speaker: Jasper van Thor

Coming soon to the department of physics: LUXD is a world unique instrument currently being commissioned in Blackett 009B. LUXD has been designed for femtosecond time resolved chemical crystallography and ultrafast solid state physics. Rather than probing single reflections in Bragg diffraction geometry, which seems to be the predominant method in both UED and time resolved X-ray diffraction in solid state physics, we are pursuing full molecular structure determination by recording all the reflections. For example a 10 Angstrom sized cell will, depending on space group symmetry, yield up to a thousand unique reflections to 1 Angstrom resolution, all of which need to be captured, scaled and merged for structure determination. title: SPC Seminar – Space – Laura Vuorinen (QMUL)
desc:
Title: Interaction of collisionless shocks and pre-existing plasma turbulence in hybrid simulations

Speaker: Laura Vuorinen (QMUL)

Abstract: Collisionless shocks and plasma turbulence play key roles in particle acceleration and energy dissipation in space plasmas. Shock waves within the heliosphere, such as planetary bow shocks and interplanetary shocks, interact with the inherently turbulent solar wind. However, historically this pre-existing turbulence has been largely neglected in plasma simulations of collisionless shocks. We present a novel modelling setup in which we generate turbulent fields in MHD simulations and dynamically input them into hybrid shock simulations, enabling us to investigate the prolonged interaction between MHD- to ion-scale plasma turbulence and a shock…

title: HEP seminar: Angela Romano (Warwick) – Recent results from the NA62 experiment at CERN
desc:
The NA62 experiment at CERN investigates rare kaon decays and searches for physics beyond the Standard Model. A major milestone is the first observation of the ultra-rare decay K + →π + νν̄, with a significance exceeding 5σ and a measured branching ratio of (13.0 +3.3 −3.0 )×10 −11 . New results from the 2023–2024 dataset, which doubles the effective sample size, provide an updated measurement with improved precision.

NA62 has also produced new preliminary results on rare and radiative kaon decays, including the first observation of K + →μ + νμ + μ − and precision measurements of K + →e + νγ and K + →π + π + π − γ.

The experiment’s broad physics programme includes searches for hidden-sector particles, such as dark photons, scalars and axion-like particles, through K + →π + X, as well…
